newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian ad agencies see 1996 turnover rise 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Italian ad agencies see 1996 turnover rise 10 pct.

text.p: Italian advertising agencies had a year of growth in 1996 and the outlook for 1997 is positive, a meeting organised by the Italian Association of Advertising Agencies (ASSAP) heard on Wednesday.

ASSAP Chairman Alberto Contri said that data on net turnover of the association's 58 members, making up 70 percent of the Italian market, showed an increase of around 10 percent in 1996 with total income of 705.18 billion lire.
The figures also showed that the "haemorrhage of staff" seen in preceding years had been stemmed with total members' personnel in 1996 totalling 3,333.

Contri said there was a process underway of re-engineering communication structures in order to better respond to the new needs of clients who were increasingly particular about consultancy services capable of supplying real added value.
"We have finally started to get down to research and development, especially in the area of new technologies," he said.
"In the struggle to keep or gain market shares in the presence of a lower demand trend, advertising companies are by now convinced that investment in communication has a decisive importance.
"This explains the 1996 increase over 1995 and gives reason to hope for a good 1997 despite the persistent possibility of stagnant demand," Contri said.
According to ASSAP data supplied by its members, the 15 leading agencies in Italy in 1996 by income were:
(Armando Testa, Media Italia, Arte Film, L'Altra, Intesta)
(Young&Rubicam Italia, Wunderman Cato Johnson, Mediapolis M&CS, G&R, S&H, Burson Marsteller)
